An analogous system in chemistry obeys the same inverse-square law; its input is scaled by a factor of 6. By the same law, the output is scaled by what factor? (A linear reading -- factor 6 -- is the distractor.)

reasoning_trace.text: Reject the surface distractor: a linear reading would give factor 6, but the law is a power of 2.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Apply the law: the input factor 6 raised to the power 2 is 6^2 = 36.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: under an inverse-square law an input factor of 6 yields an output factor of 6**2 = 36; the linear value 6 is wrong.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

final_answer: A factor of 36.

reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Apply the law: the input factor 5 raised to the power 2 is 5^2 = 25.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: under a square law an input factor of 5 yields an output factor of 5**2 = 25; the linear value 5 is wrong.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

final_answer: A factor of 25.

problem:

reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Name the distractor: by raw amount the scarcest is line L-3 (32 pollen units), which the surface reading would wrongly pick.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: By the intended relation the minimum supported count is 4, at line L-1, even though its raw stock (46) is not the smallest.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: 4 crosses consume 40 of line L-1 (<= 46), 44 of line L-2 (<= 132), 16 of line L-3 (<= 32); one more would need 50 of line L-1, exceeding 46. Mapping confirmed.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

final_answer: Line L-1 runs out first; you can complete 4 crosses.

verification.details: Binding constraint recomputed: min(stock/need) = 4 at line L-1; the raw-scarcest resource line L-3 is correctly rejected as a distractor.

problem: Consider the following. Reference system: the output follows a square law of the input -- doubling the input multiplies the output by four, so the output scales with the input raised to the power 2. An analogous system in science obeys the same square law; its input is scaled by a factor of 2. By the same law, the output is scaled by what factor? (A linear reading -- factor 2 -- is the distractor.)

reasoning_trace.text: Relation to transfer: output scales as (input)^2 (the square law), not linearly.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Reject the surface distractor: a linear reading would give factor 2, but the law is a power of 2.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Apply the law: the input factor 2 raised to the power 2 is 2^2 = 4.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: under a square law an input factor of 2 yields an output factor of 2**2 = 4; the linear value 2 is wrong.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

final_answer: A factor of 4.

verification.details: Power-law transfer verified: 2^2 = 4; linear distractor 2 rejected.

problem: Consider the following. Rule for an assembly cell: the number of kits you can complete is set by the resource with the smallest stock-divided-by-per-kit need -- which is frequently NOT the one you have least of overall. Which resource runs out first (caps the count), and how many kits do you get? (The resource you have least of by raw amount is a distractor.)

reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Compute the supported count for each: bolts = 48/4 = 12; brackets = 46/11 = 4; gaskets = 31/2 = 15 kits.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Name the distractor: by raw amount the scarcest is gaskets (31 pieces), which the surface reading would wrongly pick.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: By the intended relation the minimum supported count is 4, at brackets, even though its raw stock (46) is not the smallest.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: 4 kits consume 16 of bolts (<= 48), 44 of brackets (<= 46), 8 of gaskets (<= 31); one more would need 55 of brackets, exceeding 46. Mapping confirmed.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

final_answer: Brackets runs out first; you can complete 4 kits.

verification.details: Binding constraint recomputed: min(stock/need) = 4 at brackets; the raw-scarcest resource gaskets is correctly rejected as a distractor.
